Definition of types for identifying characteristics related to geometrical aspects of lines.

Classes

InputArea(*[, x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max])

Represents a validated rectangular area with optional boundaries.
class freeports_analysis.formats.utils.pdf_filter.pdf_parts.position.InputArea(*, x_min: Annotated[float, Gt(gt=0)] | None = None, x_max: Annotated[float, Gt(gt=0)] | None = None, y_min: Annotated[float, Gt(gt=0)] | None = None, y_max: Annotated[float, Gt(gt=0)] | None = None)

Represents a validated rectangular area with optional boundaries.

This class defines a rectangular area with optional minimum and maximum coordinates for both x and y axes. It includes validation to ensure proper coordinate ranges.

x_min

Minimum x-coordinate of the area. Must be positive if provided.

Type:

Optional[PositiveFloat]

x_max

Maximum x-coordinate of the area. Must be positive if provided.

Type:

Optional[PositiveFloat]

y_min

Minimum y-coordinate of the area. Must be positive if provided.

Type:

Optional[PositiveFloat]

y_max

Maximum y-coordinate of the area. Must be positive if provided.

Type:

Optional[PositiveFloat]

Raises:

  • ValueError – If x_max is not greater than x_min when both are provided.

  • ValueError – If y_max is not greater than y_min when both are provided.

Examples

>>> area = InputArea(x_min=0.0, x_max=10.0, y_min=0.0, y_max=5.0)
>>> area.x_min
0.0
model_config: ClassVar[ConfigDict] = {}

Configuration for the model, should be a dictionary conforming to [ConfigDict][pydantic.config.ConfigDict].

validate_bounds() → InputArea

Validate that maximum bounds are greater than minimum bounds.

This validator ensures that when both minimum and maximum values are provided for either axis, the maximum is strictly greater than the minimum.

Returns:

The validated instance.

Return type:

InputArea

Raises:

  • ValueError – If x_max is not greater than x_min when both are provided.

  • ValueError – If y_max is not greater than y_min when both are provided.
